whatItIs.heading: What lead scoring software does, and what makes it trustworthy
body: Lead scoring software assigns a number or grade to every lead so a team can work the best ones first. The mechanics are not the hard part — almost every tool on this list can produce a score.

The hard part is whether anyone believes it. A score becomes shelf furniture the moment a rep disagrees with it and cannot find out why. That happens for two reasons: the model is a black box, or the weights are so configurable that the number means whatever the last person to edit the settings decided it should mean.

So the criteria worth weighting are inspectability and stability. Can a rep open a lead and see which inputs produced the grade? Does the score update as evidence arrives, or is it stamped once at intake and left to rot? And is fit scored separately from engagement — because a strong-fit company that has gone quiet and an enthusiastic bad fit are opposite problems that a single number renders identical.

whatItIs.heading: What a startup actually needs from a CRM
body: Most CRM buying guides written for startups are really guides for the company the startup hopes to become. They weight customisation, workflow builders, reporting suites and admin controls — all of which assume somebody whose job is to own the tool.

At founder-led and first-rep scale, nobody owns the tool. The person configuring it is the person selling, and every hour spent in settings is an hour not spent on the phone. That inverts the criteria: the question is not what a system can be made to do, but what it does correctly on the first day with nothing configured.

A startup's CRM fails by being abandoned — the founder stops updating it, it drifts a fortnight out of date, and it becomes a place where leads go to be forgotten. picks.tagline: Three separate scores, continuously updated.

faqs.q: Is lead qualification software the same as lead scoring software?
faqs.a: Scoring is how most qualification software now works, so the categories overlap heavily. The distinction worth keeping is that qualification is the decision and scoring is the mechanism. A tool that scores but never updates the score is doing one-time qualification with extra steps.

faqs.q: Does qualification software replace discovery calls?
faqs.a: No. It changes which calls happen first and what the rep knows walking in. Budget, authority, need and timing still get established in conversation; the software decides which conversation is worth having this morning and keeps the record current between calls.

faqs.q: How does data quality affect qualification?
faqs.a: Directly, and most tools ignore it. A lead you cannot reliably contact is not qualified regardless of how well the company fits. In Leadkaun, Quality is scored alongside Fit and Intent and acts as a cap: a record with an invalid phone or a duplicate match is graded down no matter how strong the other two scores are.

whatItIs.heading: What lead qualification software does, and where most of it stops
body: Lead qualification software decides which enquiries are worth a rep's time. Traditionally that means a form, a set of rules and a label applied once at intake: MQL, SQL, disqualified.

The weakness is that the label is a snapshot. A lead qualifies on Monday, goes quiet for three weeks, and is still labelled SQL. Another is disqualified at intake because the form was incomplete, then replies twice asking about pricing and stays disqualified. The qualification was accurate when it was made and wrong within a fortnight, and nothing in the system notices.

The distinction worth evaluating on is whether qualification is an event or a running assessment — and whether fit and engagement are scored separately. A strong-fit company that has gone quiet and an eager buyer who will never have budget are both "medium" on a single score, and they need opposite actions.

keyTakeaways: Ask whether qualification updates as evidence arrives or is stamped once at intake — that single difference outweighs most feature comparisons.
Fit and engagement should be scored separately; collapsed into one number, opposite situations become indistinguishable.
Qualification is only as good as the data underneath it, so check what a tool does about duplicates and malformed numbers before import.
HubSpot and Salesforce offer the most configurable scoring; LeadSquared is built for high-volume lead-gen; Zoho CRM is the value option if you already run Zoho.
Leadkaun scores continuously on three dimensions and hands reps a ranked queue — it works alongside your CRM rather than replacing it.

indiaSection.heading: What qualification has to account for in Indian B2B
indiaSection.intro: Most qualification frameworks were designed around inbound email, form-fills and long written discovery. Indian B2B SMB pipelines behave differently.

points.title: Marketplace leads arrive pre-diluted
points.body: IndiaMART, JustDial and TradeIndia deliver volume with a high share of enquiries that were never going to buy. Qualification here is not a formality before routing — it is the main job.

points.title: The discovery happens on a call
points.body: Written qualification fields stay empty because the conversation was a phone call. Scoring that depends on form completeness will under-qualify most of a healthy Indian pipeline.

points.title: One buyer, several numbers
points.body: The same person enquires from a personal number, a company number and a colleague's phone. Without normalisation and deduplication, one qualified buyer looks like three ambiguous ones.

points.title: Budget is stated late
points.body: Frameworks that gate on explicit budget early tend to disqualify serious buyers who simply do not discuss price in a first call. Behaviour is the more reliable early signal.
